AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 16, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

ROLL CALL
   Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR -
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez; regarding negotiations with the Norwalk
  Association of Management Employees.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8082-013-905; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: Department of the Air Force; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  Pastor Joe Jenkins
  Florence Avenue Foursquare Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Ryan Whetstone Jr., 4th grade
  Glazier Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to proclaim Thursday, April 25, 2019 as Get on Board Day in the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to proclaim Saturday, April 27, 2019 as Arbor Day in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  Mayor’s Reorganization Recap

  2.  City of Norwalk Environmental Awareness Scholarships

  3.  2020 Census Press Conference Recap

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of April 2,
  2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period March 10, 2019 –
  March 23, 2019, in the total amount of $896,852.78. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  March 27, 2019 through April 9, 2019, in the total amount of $1,887,831.74. 640

  Report

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Martha Trejo.
  830-20

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – APRIL 10, 2019 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-11 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – Staff recommends City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 19-11, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE CITY CLERK
  DEPARTMENT. 870-02

  Report

  7.  HERMOSILLO PARK GRANT WRITING SERVICES FOR THE STATEWIDE PARK DEVELOPMENT
  AND COMMUNITY REVITALIZATION PROGRAM (PROP 68) – Staff recommends City Council
  authorize the use of Hermosillo Park Renovation funds in the amount of $11,214 for grant writing
  services to apply for Prop 68 grant funds.

  Report

  8.  APPOINTMENT OF MEMBERS OF THE CITY COUNCIL TO VARIOUS AGENCIES AND ADVISORY
  BODIES – Staff recommends City Council confirm the nominations as presented. 825-09

  Report

  9.  RESOLUTION NOS. 19-14 AND 19-15 – APPOINTMENT OF MEMBERS OF THE CITY COUNCIL TO
  THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY CITY SELECTION COMMITTEE AND THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  SANITATION DISTRICT NOS. 2 AND 18 - Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 19-14, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  DESIGNATING MAYOR MARGARITA L. RIOS AS THE CITY’S REPRESENTATIVE AND VICE
  MAYOR LUIGI VERNOLA AS THE ALTERNATE FOR THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY CITY
  SELECTION COMMITTEE/EASTERN REGION; and

  b.  Resolution No. 19-15, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPOINTING VICE MAYOR LUIGI VERNOLA AS THE CITY’S ALTERNATE TO THE
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY SANITATION DISTRICT NOS. 2 AND 18. 825-09

  Report
   10. RESOLUTION NO. 19-16 - FACSIMILE SIGNATURES - Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 19-16, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AUTHORIZING AND DIRECTING CERTAIN BANKS TO HONOR ALL CHECKS, DRAFTS, AND
  WARRANTS WHEN BEARING CERTAIN SIGNATURES AND FACSIMILE SIGNATURES OF CITY
  OFFICIALS AS DESIGNATED AND RESCINDING ALL CONFLICTING RESOLUTIONS. 602

  Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 19-17 - BUDGET AMENDMENT - AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 5 – PILOT
  SHUTTLE SERVICE - BAILMENT AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 3 – Staff recommends City
  Council:

  a.  approve Amendment No. 5 to the agreement with MV Transportation, Inc. to amend the existing
  agreement for advanced reservation services to include the provision of a pilot shuttle service for
  the period of May 6, 2019 through November 30, 2019, in the amount of $266,125;

  b.  approve Amendment No. 3 to the Bailment Agreement;

  c.  authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 5 to the agreement with MV
  Transportation, Inc. and Amendment No. 3 of the Bailment Agreement on behalf of the City, in
  forms approved by the City Attorney; and

  d.  adopt Resolution No. 19-17, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2018/19 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE PROPOSITION C FUNDS TO SUPPORT A PILOT SHUTTLE
  SERVICE, in the amount of $74,290. 610/1120-07

  Report

  12. FEDERAL TRANSIT ADMINISTRATION CERTIFICATIONS AND ASSURANCES FOR FEDERAL
  FISCAL YEAR 2019 - Staff recommends City Council authorize the Executive Director of Regional
  Transportation to execute the Fiscal Year 2019 Certifications and Assurances FTA Assistance
  Programs/Affirmation of Applicant, file a grant application on behalf of the City, and execute a grant
  agreement; in concurrence with and execution of the Affirmation of Applicant’s Attorney Certification by
  the City Attorney. 1105-01

  Report

  13. PROJECT NO. 7357 - AWARD OF CONTRACT - INSTALLATION OF CHAIN LINK FENCING ON
  ACQUIRED TANK FARM PROPERTY ADJACENT TO HOLIFIELD PARK, ENGINEERS REPORT NO.
  19-09 - Staff recommends City Council award a contract to Alcorn Fence Company of Sun Valley in the
  amount of $46,514 for the installation of chain link fencing on acquired Tank Farm property adjacent to
  Holifield Park; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments
  provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  1005-04-7357

  Report

  14. AGREEMENT RENEWAL – GENERAL SERVICES WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY – Staff
  recommends City Council approve renewal of the General Services agreement with the County of Los
  Angeles for a five-year period ending June 30, 2024, and authorize the Mayor to execute on behalf of
  the City. 125

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  15. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

  16. NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY APPOINTMENTS – Staff recommends City Council re-appoint
   Mayor Rios to a four-year term ending April 30, 2023 and Commissioner De La Garza to a two-year
  term ending April 30, 2021. 315-05-01

  Report

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  17. APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S REVOCATION OF CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO.
  934 AND ZONE VARIANCE NO. 333 - JAYNESHWAR GOUNDER, DHAKA LIQUOR AND MARKET,
  10944 IMPERIAL HIGHWAY – Direct staff as deemed appropriate. 320-01-934/320-11-333

  Report

  18. APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S DENIAL OF CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 1006
  AND PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2001 – APPLICATION FOR A RECYCLING CENTER
  LOCATED AT 11018-11030 ROSECRANS AVENUE – Direct staff as deemed appropriate. 320-01-
  1006/320-04-2001 RESOLUTIONS

  Report

  19. PROJECT NO. 7920 - RESOLUTION NO. 19-12 – LOCAL STREET PAVEMENT REHABILITATION
  PROJECT USING ROAD MAINTENANCE AND REHABILITATION ACCOUNT (RMRA) FUNDS –
  ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 19-10 - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-12, A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK ADOPTING A LIST OF
  PROJECTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 FUNDED BY SB 1: THE ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017. 1005-04-7920

  Report

REPORTS

  20. AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE ON-CALL PLANNING CONSULTING SERVICES – Staff recommends
  City Council approve an agreement with Evan Brooks Associates to provide on-call planning consulting
  services in an amount not to exceed $40,000; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

  21. UPDATE OF FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN FOR THE COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS PROGRAM – City
  Council direction is requested related to the proposed CDBG and HOME activities for the draft FY
  2019/20 Annual Action Plan. 315

  Report

  22. ENGAGEMENT OF INVESTMENT ADVISORY, MANAGEMENT AND CUSTODIAN SERVICES – Staff
  recommends City Council approve entering into an agreement with Zions Capital Advisors, Inc. for
  investment advisory and management services and Zions Bancorporation dba Zions Bank for
  custodian services; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreements, and any amendments
  provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated April 12, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
